title: Lipoprotein (a)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: A lipoprotein (a) test measures the level of lipoprotein (a) in the blood. Lipoprotein (a) is a type of LDL that carries cholesterol through the arteries, and its particles are stickier than other LDL particles.
context: Genes largely control how much lipoprotein (a) a person makes, and the level tends to stay about the same for life, so diet and exercise may not change it much. Some labs ask you to fast for 9 to 12 hours, and alcohol, niacin supplements, aspirin, or oral estrogen can affect results.
aboveRange: A high level is mostly inherited and can be associated with a higher risk of heart and blood vessel problems
Certain health conditions may affect the result
A high level can be present even when routine cholesterol levels look healthy
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
